source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה בָּֽרְבִיעִי֙ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַאֲנִ֥י בְתֽוֹךְ־הַגּוֹלָ֖ה עַל־נְהַר־כְּבָ֑ר נִפְתְּחוּ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וָאֶרְאֶ֖ה מַרְא֥וֹת אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in thirty year in the fourth, on [the] fifth of the month, and I [was] among the exiles by [the] river Kebar; were opened the heavens, and I saw visions of God.

en.L: And it came about in the thirtieth year, in the fourth [month], on the fifth [day] of the month, as I [was] among the exiles by the river Kebar, [that] the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
en.B: In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day, when I was living with the exiles beside the Kebar Canal, the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God.
en.R: It was the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month. I was living among the exiles by the Kebar Canal. The sky opened, and I saw visions from God.

pt.L: E aconteceu no trigésimo ano, no quarto [mês], no quinto [dia] do mês, estando eu entre os exilados junto ao rio Quebar, [que] os céus se abriram, e eu vi visões de Deus.
pt.B: No trigésimo ano, no quarto mês, no quinto dia, quando eu vivia com os exilados à beira do canal Quebar, os céus se abriram, e eu vi visões de Deus.
pt.R: Era o trigésimo ano, no quinto dia do quarto mês. Eu morava entre os exilados, perto do canal Quebar. O céu se abriu, e eu vi visões que vinham de Deus.

es.L: Y sucedió en el año treinta, en el [mes] cuarto, el [día] cinco del mes, estando yo entre los desterrados junto al río Quebar, [que] se abrieron los cielos, y vi visiones de Dios.
es.B: En el año treinta, en el mes cuarto, el día cinco, cuando yo vivía con los desterrados junto al canal Quebar, se abrieron los cielos y vi visiones de Dios.
es.R: Era el año treinta, el día cinco del mes cuarto. Yo vivía entre los desterrados junto al canal Quebar. El cielo se abrió, y vi visiones que venían de Dios.

sw.L: Ikawa katika mwaka wa thelathini, katika [mwezi] wa nne, [siku] ya tano ya mwezi, nilipokuwa katikati ya wahamishwa kando ya mto Kebari, mbingu zikafunguliwa, nami nikaona maono ya Mungu.
sw.B: Katika mwaka wa thelathini, mwezi wa nne, siku ya tano, nilipokuwa nikiishi pamoja na wahamishwa kando ya mfereji wa Kebari, mbingu zilifunguliwa nami nikaona maono ya Mungu.
sw.R: Ilikuwa mwaka wa thelathini, siku ya tano ya mwezi wa nne. Nilikuwa nikiishi pamoja na watu waliopelekwa uhamishoni, kando ya mfereji wa Kebari. Anga likafunguka, nami nikaona maono kutoka kwa Mungu.

ko.L: 제30년 넷째 [달] 그달 오일에, 내가 그발 강 가에서 포로들 가운데 있었는데, 하늘이 열리고 나는 하나님의 환상들을 보았다.
ko.B: 30년째 되는 해 넷째 달 오일에, 내가 그발 운하 가에서 포로들과 함께 살고 있을 때에, 하늘이 열리고 나는 하나님의 환상들을 보았다.
ko.R: 30년째 되는 해 넷째 달 오일이었다. 나는 그발 운하 가에서 포로로 끌려온 사람들과 함께 살고 있었다. 그때 하늘이 열리고, 나는 하나님께서 보여 주시는 환상을 보았다.

vi.L: Và đã xảy ra vào năm thứ ba mươi, [tháng] thứ tư, ngày mồng năm trong tháng, khi tôi [đang ở] giữa những người lưu đày bên sông Kê-ba, các tầng trời mở ra, và tôi thấy những khải tượng của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Vào ngày mồng năm tháng tư năm thứ ba mươi, khi tôi đang sống với những người lưu đày bên kênh Kê-ba, các tầng trời mở ra và tôi thấy những khải tượng của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Đó là năm thứ ba mươi, ngày mồng năm tháng tư. Tôi đang sống giữa những người lưu đày bên kênh Kê-ba. Bầu trời mở ra, và tôi thấy những khải tượng từ Đức Chúa Trời.

fr.L: Et il arriva, la trentième année, au quatrième [mois], le cinq du mois, comme j’[étais] parmi les exilés près du fleuve Kebar, [que] les cieux s’ouvrirent, et je vis des visions de Dieu.
fr.B: La trentième année, le quatrième mois, le cinquième jour, alors que je vivais parmi les exilés au bord du canal de Kebar, les cieux s’ouvrirent et je vis des visions de Dieu.
fr.R: C’était la trentième année, le cinquième jour du quatrième mois. Je vivais parmi les exilés, au bord du canal de Kebar. Le ciel s’est ouvert, et j’ai vu des visions envoyées par Dieu.

am.L: በሠላሳኛውም ዓመት፣ በአራተኛው [ወር]፣ ከወሩም በአምስተኛው [ቀን] እንዲህ ሆነ፤ እኔ በኮቦር ወንዝ አጠገብ በምርኮኞች መካከል ሳለሁ ሰማያት ተከፈቱ፤ የእግዚአብሔርንም ራእዮች አየሁ።
am.B: በሠላሳኛው ዓመት፣ በአራተኛው ወር፣ በአምስተኛው ቀን፣ በኮቦር ቦይ አጠገብ ከምርኮኞቹ ጋር እኖር በነበረ ጊዜ ሰማይ ተከፈተ፤ የእግዚአብሔርንም ራእዮች አየሁ።
am.R: ጊዜው ሠላሳኛው ዓመት፣ የአራተኛው ወር አምስተኛ ቀን ነበር። እኔ በኮቦር ቦይ አጠገብ በምርኮኞች መካከል እኖር ነበር። ሰማዩ ተከፈተ፤ ከእግዚአብሔር የመጡ ራእዮችንም አየሁ።

hi.L: और ऐसा हुआ कि तीसवें वर्ष में, चौथे [महीने] में, महीने के पाँचवें [दिन], जब मैं कबार नदी के किनारे निर्वासितों के बीच [था], आकाश खुल गया, और मैंने परमेश्वर के दर्शन देखे।
hi.B: तीसवें वर्ष के चौथे महीने के पाँचवें दिन, जब मैं कबार नहर के किनारे निर्वासितों के साथ रहता था, आकाश खुल गया और मैंने परमेश्वर के दर्शन देखे।
hi.R: यह तीसवाँ वर्ष था, चौथे महीने का पाँचवाँ दिन। मैं कबार नहर के किनारे निर्वासित लोगों के बीच रहता था। आकाश खुल गया, और मैंने परमेश्वर की ओर से दर्शन देखे।

ru.L: И было: в тридцатый год, в четвёртый [месяц], в пятый [день] месяца, когда я [был] среди изгнанников у реки Ховар, открылись небеса, и я увидел видения Божьи.
ru.B: В тридцатый год, в четвёртый месяц, в пятый день, когда я жил среди изгнанников у канала Ховар, открылись небеса, и я увидел видения Божьи.
ru.R: Шёл тридцатый год, пятый день четвёртого месяца. Я жил среди изгнанников у канала Ховар. Небо открылось, и я увидел видения от Бога.

ja.L: 第三十年の第四[の月]、その月の五日のことである。わたしがケバル川のほとりで捕囚の民の中にいたとき、天が開かれ、わたしは神の幻を見た。
ja.B: 第三十年の第四の月の五日、わたしがケバル運河のほとりで捕囚の民と共に暮らしていたとき、天が開かれ、わたしは神の幻を見た。
ja.R: それは、第三十年の第四の月の五日のことでした。わたしは、ケバル運河のほとりで、捕虜として連れて来られた人々の中で暮らしていました。すると、空が開け、わたしは神からの幻を見ました。

uk.L: І сталося в тридцятому році, у четвертому [місяці], пʼятого [дня] місяця, коли я [був] серед вигнанців біля ріки Кевар, [що] небеса відкрилися, і я побачив видіння Божі.
uk.B: У тридцятому році, четвертого місяця, пʼятого дня, коли я жив серед вигнанців біля каналу Кевар, небеса відкрилися, і я побачив видіння Божі.
uk.R: Це було в тридцятому році, пʼятого дня четвертого місяця. Я жив серед вигнанців біля каналу Кевар. Небо відкрилося, і я побачив видіння від Бога.

decisions.choice: the thirtieth year: a date whose starting point is not given
alternatives: the thirtieth year of the exile, when the book was finished
decisions.reason: The book's other dates count the years of King Jehoiachin's exile (verse 2; 8:1; 33:21; 40:1), but this one gives no starting point, and verse 2 adds the usual reckoning beside it. The most common reading takes it as Ezekiel's age: he was a priest (verse 3), and priests began their full service at thirty (Numbers 4:3). Others count from the finding of the book of the law under Josiah in 622 BC (2 Kings 22:8), which also gives 593 BC, or take it as the year the book was finished. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the river Kebar: a canal of the Euphrates in Babylonia
decisions.reason: Kebar is not one of the great rivers. Babylonian business records of the fifth century BC name a large canal of this name near the city of Nippur, south of Babylon, which carried water from the Euphrates. The exiles from Judah were settled along it, at Tel-abib (3:15). The word translated "river" is used for canals as well as rivers (Psalm 137:1, "by the rivers of Babylon").

decisions.choice: visions of God: visions that God gave, which show God's glory
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean visions that come from God or visions in which God is seen, and both are true here: the vision is God's gift and shows his glory (verse 28). The same phrase opens the later visions of 8:3 and 40:2.

decisions.choice: And it came about ... I: the book opens with Ezekiel speaking for himself
decisions.reason: The book begins with "And it came about", as many books of narrative do (Joshua 1:1; Ruth 1:1); it is a way of starting an account, not a link to something before it. Ezekiel tells the vision in the first person, and verses 2-3 then step in with a note in the third person.

decisions.choice: the river Kebar (L); the Kebar Canal (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "river", the word the text uses. Balanced and Readable say "canal", which is what the Kebar was (m2), so that readers do not look for it on a map of rivers. Readable says "the sky opened" for "the heavens were opened" (the same word means both) and "visions from God" for the sense in m3.

decisions.choice: in the fourth month, on the fifth day (B); on the fifth day of the fourth month (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives the month and then the day, and leaves "month" and "day" to be understood; Literal brackets them. Balanced keeps the Hebrew order and says "month" and "day"; Readable gives the date in the order English usually uses, and splits the long sentence into short ones.

decisions.choice: no Nº ano, no Nº [mês], no Nº [dia] do mês (L); no Nº ano, no Nº mês, no Nº dia (B); no Nº dia do Nº mês (R)
alternatives: no dia cinco do mês quatro
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Ezekiel's dates (1:1-2; 8:1; 20:1; 24:1; 26:1; 29:1, 17; 30:20; 31:1; 32:1, 17; 33:21; 40:1) keep one wording at each level, with ordinal numbers in words, as 2 Kings 25:27 gives a date in Portuguese ("no trigésimo sétimo ano ... no décimo segundo mês"). Literal brackets "mês" and "dia", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood; Balanced keeps the Hebrew order of month and day; Readable gives the day first, "no quinto dia do quarto mês", as the English Readable does (r-en-2).

decisions.choice: o rio Quebar (L); o canal Quebar (B, R); visões de Deus
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 1:3; 3:15, 23; 10:15, 20, 22; 43:3): the name is written as Portuguese writes its sounds, "Quebar", since Portuguese spells a hard k before e with "qu". Literal keeps "rio", the word the text uses; Balanced and Readable say "canal", which is what the Kebar was (m2), as the English does. "Visões de Deus" keeps both senses the meaning note gives (m3); Readable says they came from God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "el río Quebar" (L); "el canal Quebar" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Spanish spells the name with Qu-, as Spanish writes the Hebrew k elsewhere; book-wide in Ezekiel. "Canal" at B and R, as the English, because it was an irrigation canal

decisions.choice: "los desterrados"
decisions.reason: The exiles (golah) are "los desterrados" at every level, the published word for people taken into exile (Deuteronomy 30:4; 2 Kings)

decisions.choice: mto Kebari (L); mfereji wa Kebari (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Kebar was a canal of the Euphrates (meaning decision); Literal keeps "river", and Balanced and Readable say "mfereji", canal, as the English does and as the Swahili Ezra words the Ahava. One wording for the whole book.

decisions.choice: wahamishwa (L, B); watu waliopelekwa uhamishoni (R)
decisions.reason: The exile community in Babylonia is "wahamishwa", the word the published Isaiah 20:4 uses; Readable spells out "people taken into exile". Kept for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "제30년" (L); "30년째 되는 해" (B, R), in figures; the month and day in words ("넷째 달 오일")
decisions.reason: Years in figures and months and days in words, as the Kings formula and the Ezekiel term sheet set for dated headings in Korean.

decisions.choice: "그발 강" (L); "그발 운하" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide for Ezekiel: the published Protestant form of the name, with "운하" (canal) where the English says "Canal".

decisions.choice: năm thứ ba mươi, tháng thứ tư, ngày mồng năm (L); ngày mồng năm tháng tư năm thứ ba mươi (B); năm thứ ba mươi, ngày mồng năm tháng tư (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order year, month, day. Balanced and Readable give the date as Vietnamese writes it, day before month; days one to ten take "mồng". This holds for every dated heading in Ezekiel. "sông Kê-ba" (L) and "kênh Kê-ba" (B, R) follow the English river/canal choice.

decisions.choice: Ezekiel's first-person narrative: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("les cieux s'ouvrirent", "je vis"), passé composé at Readable ("le ciel s'est ouvert", "j'ai vu"); God's words to him, being speech, use present, future and passé composé at every level. For chapters 1-11
decisions.reason: The French style guide and the term sheet for these books treat Ezekiel's visions and frames as narrative told in the first person, like Revelation ("je vis" at Literal and Balanced, "j'ai vu" at Readable), while the oracles are speech.

decisions.choice: "le fleuve Kebar" (Literal); "le canal de Kebar" (Balanced, Readable), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The French follows the English distinction: the Hebrew word is "river", kept at Literal, while Balanced and Readable name what Kebar was, a canal of the Euphrates. The name is written "Kebar", the form fixed in the term sheet for these books.

decisions.choice: Elohim "እግዚአብሔር" in this book where it names the one God ("የእግዚአብሔር ራእዮች", visions of God); "አምላክ" with a possessor ("አምላካቸው") or for a god; Kebar "ኮቦር": "የኮቦር ወንዝ" (Literal), "የኮቦር ቦይ" (Balanced, Readable); the exiles (golah) "ምርኮኞች"
decisions.reason: As the style brief (7a) asks, the first record of the book says how Elohim is given. Balanced and Readable follow the English "Kebar Canal" (the meaning decision: a canal off the Euphrates) with "ቦይ", the Amharic word for a dug watercourse; Literal keeps "river". The exiles are "ምርኮኞች", as in Kings and Ezra.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of this chapter
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader setting that capitalizes pronouns referring to God has nothing to change in Amharic; the English spans in this chapter (from verse 3) have no Amharic counterpart.

decisions.choice: कबार नदी (L); कबार नहर (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "river" (nahar), the word the text uses. The Kebar was a canal of the Euphrates (m2), so Balanced and Readable say नहर, as the English says "canal". This is the form for the Kebar through the whole book.

decisions.choice: निर्वासित (exiles)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel lives among the people deported from Judah with King Jehoiachin. निर्वासित, "exiled", is the word the Hindi history books use for the exile of Jehoiachin (2 Kings 25:27 निर्वासन), so the exiles are निर्वासित at every level.

decisions.choice: "река Ховар" (L); "канал Ховар" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The traditional Russian form of the name is Ховар, and it is used throughout Ezekiel. Literal keeps "река", the word the text uses; Balanced and Readable say "канал", which is what the Kebar was (m2), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "изгнанники" for the exiles (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The book's word for the people taken to Babylon with Jehoiachin. "Изгнанники" says that they were driven from their land; "плен" is kept for the captivity itself (as in Ezra).

decisions.choice: Book-wide register for Ezekiel, following the prophetic conventions of Isaiah and Jeremiah: Ezekiel's narrative frame is plain style (だ・である) at Literal and Balanced and です・ます at Readable, with light respect forms for God only; Ezekiel narrates himself as "わたし"; God's speech is plain at every level and never uses a respect form of himself.
alternatives: です・ます in the narrative at every level
decisions.reason: The same register rules as Isaiah and Jeremiah (narrative plain at L, B; polite at R), so the prophets read alike; see notes/EZK-EZK-1.md, EZEKIEL CONVENTIONS.

decisions.choice: "ケバル川" (L), "ケバル運河" (B, R), as the English river / Canal; the exiles "捕囚の民" (L, B), "捕虜として連れて来られた人々" (R).
decisions.reason: The Kebar was a canal of the Euphrates (m2); Ezra 8:15 has the same pattern (アハワ川 / アハワ運河). "捕囚の民" is the form of Ezra and Daniel for haggolah; Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: Book-wide names: "Єзекіїл", "Бузі", "Кевар", "Єгояхин", "халдеї" (L, B) / "вавилоняни" (R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel follows the Old Testament terms note; the other names are transcribed with в for the Hebrew b as Ukrainian does (Авраам, Вавилон) and are kept through the book. Readable names the Chaldeans as Babylonians, as the English Readable does.

source.text: בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הִ֚יא הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: On [the] fifth of the month, it [was] the year the fifth of the exile of the king Jehoiachin,

en.L: on the fifth of the month, that [was] the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin,
en.B: on the fifth day of the month (this was the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile),
en.R: This was in the fifth year after King Jehoiachin had been taken away as a prisoner.

pt.L: no quinto [dia] do mês, que [era] o quinto ano do exílio do rei Joaquim,
pt.B: no quinto dia do mês (era o quinto ano do exílio do rei Joaquim),
pt.R: Isso aconteceu no quinto ano depois que o rei Joaquim tinha sido levado como prisioneiro.

es.L: el cinco del mes, ese [era] el año quinto del destierro del rey Joaquín,
es.B: el día cinco del mes (era el quinto año del destierro del rey Joaquín),
es.R: Esto fue en el quinto año después de que el rey Joaquín fuera llevado prisionero.

sw.L: katika [siku] ya tano ya mwezi, huo [ulikuwa] mwaka wa tano wa uhamisho wa mfalme Yehoyakini,
sw.B: siku ya tano ya mwezi (huo ulikuwa mwaka wa tano wa uhamisho wa mfalme Yehoyakini),
sw.R: Huo ulikuwa mwaka wa tano tangu mfalme Yehoyakini alipochukuliwa kama mfungwa.

decisions.choice: the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin: 593 BC
decisions.reason: Jehoiachin, king of Judah, was taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC, after a reign of three months, together with the leading people of Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:8-16). Ezekiel was evidently among them. His fifth year of exile was 593 BC, and the fourth month of that year (verse 1) fell in early summer, about July. Ezekiel dates his visions and messages by the years of this exile (8:1; 20:1; 33:21; 40:1), as if the exiled king were still the rightful one.

decisions.choice: it was the fifth year: a note that gives the date by the usual reckoning
decisions.reason: Verses 2-3 speak of Ezekiel in the third person, as a note added to his own words in verse 1. They repeat the day of the month and give the year in the reckoning the rest of the book uses, so that the uncertain "thirtieth year" can be placed. The sentence runs on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: the year in parentheses (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced sets the year in parentheses because it breaks into the sentence, as the Hebrew does. The record ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced, because the sentence goes on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: after King Jehoiachin had been taken away as a prisoner
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the exile of King Jehoiachin": he had been taken away from his land as a prisoner. Readable gives the day once, in verse 1, and makes this a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: Joaquim
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the king exiled in 597 BC (m1) is "Joaquim", the form 2 Kings 24:8-15 and 25:27 give Jehoiachin in Portuguese, kept apart from his father Jehoiakim, "Jeoaquim" (Jeremiah 1:3). The exile is "o exílio" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what it was, as the English Readable does (r-en-2).

decisions.choice: "Joaquín"
decisions.reason: The king is "Joaquín", the form published in 2 Kings 24–25 and 2 Chronicles 36

decisions.choice: "Joïakin" for Jehoiachin
decisions.reason: The form already published for this king in Kings and Jeremiah, fixed in the term sheet for these books.

decisions.choice: राजा यहोयाकीन के निर्वासन का पाँचवाँ वर्ष (L, B); राजा यहोयाकीन के बंदी बनाकर ले जाए जाने के बाद का पाँचवाँ वर्ष (R)
decisions.reason: Jehoiachin keeps the form of 2 Kings 24-25 (यहोयाकीन), and his exile is निर्वासन, as 2 Kings 25:27 has it. Readable spells out what the exile was, as the English Readable does. Ezekiel dates his book by this exile, so the same wording should be used at each later date (8:1 and onward).

decisions.choice: "Иехония" for Jehoiachin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here has a short form of the king's name, but it is the same king as in 2 Kings 24-25, where the Russian draft calls him Иехония; the same form is kept so that readers know him.

decisions.choice: 1:2 made a full sentence in each level, with "ヨヤキン" (2 Kings 24, Jeremiah); Balanced uses "すなわち" for the English parentheses.
alternatives: parentheses at B as the English
decisions.reason: The English runs 1:1-3 into one sentence; Japanese would have to move the date after the verb of 1:1, so each verse is its own sentence. The parenthesis is not needed in Japanese.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was on him: the LORD's power took hold of him
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power. The phrase is used when the LORD's power seizes a prophet to make him act or to show him a vision (1 Kings 18:46; 2 Kings 3:15). In Ezekiel it comes before each of the great visions (3:14, 22; 8:1; 33:22; 37:1; 40:1), and it marks what follows as the LORD's doing, not the prophet's own.

decisions.choice: surely came: the word came, and came truly
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, a common Hebrew way of saying that something really happened. The note insists that what Ezekiel saw and heard far from the temple, in a foreign land, was a real word from the LORD.

decisions.choice: Ezekiel the priest: Ezekiel himself was a priest
alternatives: Buzi the priest: his father was the priest
decisions.reason: The word "the priest" can belong to Ezekiel or to his father Buzi, but it is usually taken of Ezekiel, and the book bears it out: he knows the temple and its rules closely (chapters 8; 40-48) and is careful about ritual purity (4:14). He belonged to the priestly families taken to Babylon with Jehoiachin. His name means "God strengthens" or "may God make strong", and God's promise to make him hard and strong against the people (3:8-9) seems to play on it.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon him (L); came on him (B); the power of the LORD came on him (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Ezekiel: Literal says "was upon", Balanced "came on", and Readable says what the hand stands for (m1), as 2 Kings 3:15 does. Ezekiel's later accounts use the same words in the first person ("upon me", "on me").

decisions.choice: spoke his word (R); the Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the LORD the subject of the sentence ("spoke his word to"), which says the same as "the word of the LORD came to" in plainer English. It says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans", as in Isaiah and Jeremiah, and names Ezekiel again so that the long sentence can be split.

decisions.choice: a mão do SENHOR estava sobre (L); veio sobre (B); o poder do SENHOR veio sobre (R)
alternatives: a mão do SENHOR pousou sobre
decisions.reason: For the whole book (3:14, 22; 8:1; 33:22; 37:1; 40:1): the formula (m1) keeps one wording at each level, as the English does (r-en-1): Literal "a mão do SENHOR estava sobre", Balanced "veio sobre", and Readable says what the hand stands for, "o poder do SENHOR", with the same verb as Balanced.

decisions.choice: Ezequiel, filho de Buzi; certamente veio (L); os caldeus (L, B), os babilônios (R); deu a sua mensagem (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the prophet is "Ezequiel", the usual Brazilian form, and "filho de" stands between commas, as Isaiah 1:1 and Jeremiah 1:1 name their prophets. Literal says the doubled verb (m2) with "certamente", as the English says "surely". The Chaldeans are "os caldeus" at Literal and Balanced and "os babilônios" at Readable, as Isaiah and Jeremiah have them. Readable says that the LORD gave his message, the Readable wording Jeremiah 1:4 sets for the word-event formula.

decisions.choice: "la mano del SEÑOR estuvo sobre él" (L); "la mano del SEÑOR vino sobre él" (B); "el poder del SEÑOR vino sobre él" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide wording for the formula, as 2 Kings 3:15 in Spanish

decisions.choice: "los caldeos" (L, B); "los babilonios" (R)
decisions.reason: As published for the Chaldeans as a people (2 Kings 25)

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span; God takes the honorific ("주셨다", "께서", "그분") at every level
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change; respect for God is carried by the honorific throughout Ezekiel (Korean style guide 7).

decisions.choice: "$DN의 손이 그 위에 있었다" (L); "…손이 그에게 임했다" (B); "$DN의 능력이 그에게 내렸다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Ezekiel term sheet's wording for "the hand of the LORD was on me", used wherever the formula recurs, as 2 Kings 3:15.

decisions.choice: tay của CHÚA ở trên (L); tay của CHÚA đặt trên (B); quyền năng của CHÚA đến trên (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of 1 Kings 18:46 and 2 Kings 3:15, kept through Ezekiel. Readable says what the idiom means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: người Canh-đê (L, B); người Ba-by-lôn (R)
decisions.reason: As in Jeremiah and 2 Kings 25: Readable names the people by the empire readers know.

decisions.choice: "Ézéchiel fils de Bouzi", for the whole book
alternatives: "Ezéchiel" without the accent on the capital
decisions.reason: The usual French form of the prophet's name, with the accented capital the style guide asks for, as fixed in the term sheet.

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR a parlé au prêtre Ézéchiel" (Readable), with no pronoun span
alternatives: "le SEIGNEUR a adressé sa parole à Ézéchiel"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's Readable wording for this verse. French needs no possessive here, so the English Readable's "his" span has no French counterpart.

decisions.choice: mkono wa BWANA ulikuwa juu yangu (L); mkono wa BWANA ukanijia (B); nguvu ya BWANA ikanijia (R)
alternatives: mkono wa BWANA at every level
decisions.reason: The formula returns through Ezekiel (3:14, 22; 8:1; 37:1; 40:1) and keeps this wording at each level, as the published 2 Kings 3:15. Readable says plainly that the LORD's power took hold of him (meaning decision). Ezekieli mwana wa Buzi and Wakaldayo (L, B) / Wababeli (R) are the book-wide forms of the terms note.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives that mean God, mid-sentence ("neno lake", "nami", "kwangu"), never on verb prefixes
alternatives: a span on every pronoun, as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("alimpa", "ukamjia"), and a verb prefix or object marker cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun span stands only on free pronouns and possessives ("neno lake", "kiuno chake"). Ezekiel therefore has fewer spans in Swahili than in English. Mid-sentence, every free pronoun or possessive that means God takes the span, including "nami", "naye", "yeye" and "kwangu"; a word that opens a sentence is written plainly with its capital, and "naye" followed by a noun ("naye BWANA") is a conjunction with no span. This holds for the whole book.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon him "{{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} እጅ በእርሱ ላይ ነበረች" (Literal, Balanced); "{{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ኃይል ያዘው" (Readable)
alternatives: "... እጅ መጣችበት" (Balanced, after the English "came on him")
decisions.reason: The formula recurs in Ezekiel (3:14, 22; 8:1; 37:1; 40:1) and is given one wording through the book: Literal and Balanced keep the hand, as the Ezekiel terms list has it; Readable says what it means, the LORD's power took hold of him (the English "the power of the LORD came on him"), with the natural Amharic verb "ያዘው".

decisions.choice: Ezekiel "ሕዝቅኤል"; Buzi "ቡዚ"; Jehoiachin "ዮአኪን" (verse 2, as Kings); the Chaldeans "ከለዳውያን" (Literal, Balanced), "ባቢሎናውያን" (Readable); "surely came" "በእርግጥ መጣ" (Literal only)
decisions.reason: Names keep the forms used in Kings and Jeremiah. Literal marks the Hebrew's doubled verb (the meaning decision) with "በእርግጥ"; Balanced and Readable leave it in the plain "መጣ", as the English does.

decisions.choice: प्रभु for both YHWH and Adonai; the divine_name setting tells them apart
decisions.reason: Hindi uses प्रभु both for the name YHWH ("the LORD") and for Adonai ("Lord"). Every YHWH is a divine_name span (प्रभु by default, याहवे as the alternative), and "the Lord GOD" (Adonai YHWH) is प्रभु {{divine_name:परमेश्वर|याहवे}}, so a reader who switches the setting sees which is which. यहोवा is not used.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} का हाथ उस पर था (L); उस पर आया (B); {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की सामर्थ उस पर आई (R)
alternatives: प्रभु की आत्मा उस पर आया
decisions.reason: The hand of the LORD is his power taking hold of the prophet (m1). Literal and Balanced keep "hand", as 2 Kings 3:15 does for Elisha; Readable says सामर्थ, as 2 Kings 3:15 does at that level. This wording is kept wherever the phrase returns (3:14, 3:22, 8:1).

decisions.choice: बाबुलियों का देश (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep कसदी, the form 2 Kings and Daniel use for the Chaldeans. Readable names them by their country, as the English Readable says "Babylonians": बाबुली, as 2 Kings and Jeremiah at Readable.

decisions.choice: सचमुच (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb ("coming, it came") to stress that the word really came (m2). Literal keeps that with सचमुच; Balanced and Readable leave it in the plain statement, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "была на нём рука ГОСПОДА" (L); "сошла на него рука ГОСПОДА" (B); "сошла на него сила ГОСПОДА" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Ezekiel, as 2 Kings 3:15: Literal keeps "was upon", Balanced says "came on" (сошла), and Readable says what the hand stands for, the LORD's power (m1).

decisions.choice: "И было слово ГОСПОДА к ..." (L); "ГОСПОДЬ обратился к ..." (B); "ГОСПОДЬ дал ... слово" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set for all the prophets. Literal adds "истинно" for the doubled verb (m2). Readable has "дал своё слово" here because no speech follows; where one does, it is "дал ... такое слово". The English "his" for God becomes the reflexive "своё", which takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "Иезекииль, сын Вузия"
decisions.reason: The traditional Russian forms of the prophet's and his father's names.

decisions.choice: The hand of the LORD (a book-wide formula, 3:14, 22; 8:1; 33:22; 37:1; 40:1): "主の手が彼の上にあった" (L), "主の手が彼に臨んだ" (B), "主の力がエゼキエルに臨みました" (R).
decisions.reason: The same forms as 2 Kings 3:15 (手が臨んだ / 力が臨みました); Literal keeps "upon" (上にあった), Readable follows the English "the power of the LORD" (m1).

decisions.choice: Names: "ブジの子エゼキエル" (L, B), "ブジの息子エゼキエル" (R); the Chaldeans "カルデア人" (L, B), "バビロニア人" (R, as the English R).
decisions.reason: Ezekiel is エゼキエル, the usual Japanese form of the name; 'son of' follows the historical books (L, B の子, R 息子). The Chaldeans keep the Jeremiah and Daniel form.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}" in capitals, inflected inside each option, for the divine name; "Владика {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}" for Adonai YHWH
decisions.reason: As the Old Testament terms note settles: the capitals mirror the English "the LORD" and keep the name apart from Adonai, "Господь" in ordinary letters, so the setting tells the two apart; the alternative gives "Ягве". Ezekiel's constant "the Lord GOD" is "Владика {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}", so the two words do not read "Lord LORD", as in the Ukrainian Exodus and Deuteronomy. Book-wide choice.

decisions.choice: "рука [ГОСПОДА] була на ньому" (L); "зійшла рука" (B); "зійшла сила" (R)
decisions.reason: Following the Ezekiel terms table: Readable says what the hand means, the LORD's power, as in 2 Kings 3:15. The same wording is kept at 3:14, 3:22, 8:1, 33:22, 37:1 and 40:1.

source.text: וָאֵ֡רֶא וְהִנֵּה֩ ר֨וּחַ סְעָרָ֜ה בָּאָ֣ה מִן־הַצָּפ֗וֹן עָנָ֤ן גָּדוֹל֙ וְאֵ֣שׁ מִתְלַקַּ֔חַת וְנֹ֥גַֽהּ ל֖וֹ סָבִ֑יב וּמִ֨תּוֹכָ֔הּ כְּעֵ֥ין הַחַשְׁמַ֖ל מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I looked, and see, a wind of storm coming from the north, a cloud great and fire taking hold of itself, and brightness to it all around, and from its midst like [the] appearance of the chashmal, from [the] midst of the fire.

en.L: And I looked, and see, a stormy wind was coming from the north, a great cloud, and fire flashing back and forth, and brightness [was] all around it, and from its midst [there was something] like the appearance of amber, from the midst of the fire.
en.B: As I looked, I saw a storm wind coming from the north: a huge cloud with fire flashing through it and brightness all around it. In the middle of the fire was something that looked like gleaming metal.
en.R: I looked and saw a windstorm coming from the north. There was a huge cloud with fire flashing in it, and a bright light shone all around it. In the middle of the fire was something that looked like shining metal.

pt.L: E olhei, e eis que um vento tempestuoso vinha do norte, uma grande nuvem, e fogo que lampejava sem cessar, e um resplendor ao redor dela, e do meio dela [havia algo] como a aparência de âmbar, do meio do fogo.
pt.B: Olhei e vi um vento de tempestade que vinha do norte: uma nuvem enorme, com fogo lampejando dentro dela e um resplendor ao seu redor. No meio do fogo havia algo que parecia metal reluzente.
pt.R: Olhei e vi uma tempestade de vento que vinha do norte. Havia uma nuvem enorme com fogo brilhando dentro dela, e uma luz forte brilhava ao redor dela. No meio do fogo havia uma coisa que parecia metal brilhante.

es.L: Y miré, y he aquí, un viento tempestuoso venía del norte, una gran nube, y fuego que fulguraba sin cesar, y resplandor [había] alrededor de ella, y de en medio de ella [había algo] como el aspecto del ámbar, de en medio del fuego.
es.B: Miré y vi un viento de tormenta que venía del norte: una nube enorme con fuego que relampagueaba en ella y un resplandor a su alrededor. En medio del fuego había algo que parecía metal reluciente.
es.R: Miré y vi una tormenta que venía del norte. Había una nube enorme con fuego que relampagueaba dentro, y una luz brillante la rodeaba. En medio del fuego había algo que parecía metal brillante.

sw.L: Nikatazama, na tazama, upepo wa dhoruba ulikuwa ukija kutoka kaskazini, wingu kubwa, na moto ukimulika huku na huku, na mwangaza [ulikuwa] pande zote kulizunguka, na kutoka katikati yake [kulikuwa na kitu] kama sura ya kaharabu, kutoka katikati ya moto.
sw.B: Nilipotazama, niliona upepo wa dhoruba ukija kutoka kaskazini: wingu kubwa lenye moto ukimulika ndani yake, na mwangaza pande zote kulizunguka. Katikati ya moto kulikuwa na kitu kilichoonekana kama madini yanayong'aa.
sw.R: Nilitazama nikaona dhoruba ya upepo ikija kutoka kaskazini. Kulikuwa na wingu kubwa lenye moto unaomulika ndani yake, na mwanga mkali uliangaza pande zote kulizunguka. Katikati ya moto kulikuwa na kitu kilichoonekana kama chuma kinachong'aa.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 보니, 보라, 폭풍이 북쪽에서 오고 있었다. 큰 구름과 번쩍이는 불이 있고 그 둘레에 광채가 있었으며, 그 가운데서, 곧 불 가운데서 호박금의 모습 같은 것이 [보였다].
ko.B: 내가 바라보니, 폭풍이 북쪽에서 불어오고 있었다. 큰 구름 속에서 불이 번쩍이고, 그 둘레에는 광채가 빛나고 있었다. 그 불 한가운데에는 빛나는 금속처럼 보이는 것이 있었다.
ko.R: 내가 보니, 북쪽에서 폭풍이 불어왔다. 큰 구름 속에서 불이 번쩍였고, 그 둘레에는 밝은 빛이 비쳤다. 그 불 한가운데에 반짝이는 금속처럼 보이는 것이 있었다.

vi.L: Và tôi nhìn, và kìa, một cơn gió bão đang đến từ phương bắc, một đám mây lớn, và lửa lóe chớp liên hồi, và ánh sáng chói [bao] quanh nó, và từ giữa nó [có vật gì] như diện mạo của hổ phách, từ giữa lửa.
vi.B: Tôi nhìn và thấy một trận gió bão từ phương bắc thổi đến: một đám mây khổng lồ, có lửa lóe chớp xuyên qua và ánh sáng chói rực bao quanh. Giữa lửa có một vật trông giống như kim loại sáng loáng.
vi.R: Tôi nhìn và thấy một cơn bão từ phương bắc kéo đến. Có một đám mây rất lớn, lửa lóe chớp trong đó, và ánh sáng chói chiếu ra khắp chung quanh. Ở giữa lửa có một vật trông giống như kim loại chiếu sáng.

fr.L: Et je regardai, et voici, un vent de tempête venait du nord, une grande nuée, et un feu qui jaillissait sans cesse, et une clarté [était] tout autour d’elle, et du milieu d’elle [il y avait] comme l’aspect de l’ambre, du milieu du feu.
fr.B: Je regardai, et je vis un vent de tempête venir du nord : une énorme nuée traversée d’un feu qui jaillissait, et entourée de clarté. Au milieu du feu, il y avait quelque chose qui ressemblait à un métal étincelant.
fr.R: J’ai regardé, et j’ai vu une tempête qui arrivait du nord. Il y avait un énorme nuage, avec du feu qui jaillissait dedans, et une lumière brillait tout autour. Au milieu du feu, il y avait quelque chose qui ressemblait à un métal qui brille.

am.L: እኔም አየሁ፤ እነሆም፣ አውሎ ነፋስ ከሰሜን ይመጣ ነበር፤ ታላቅ ደመናና ወዲያና ወዲህ የሚብለጨለጭ እሳት [ነበረ]፤ በዙሪያውም ብርሃን [ነበረ]፤ ከመካከሉም፣ ከእሳቱ መካከል፣ እንደ ቢጫ ዕንቁ መልክ ያለ [ነገር ነበረ]።
am.B: ስመለከትም ከሰሜን አውሎ ነፋስ ሲመጣ አየሁ፤ እሳት የሚብለጨለጭበት ታላቅ ደመና ነበረ፤ በዙሪያውም ብርሃን ነበረ። በእሳቱም መካከል የሚያንጸባርቅ ብረት የሚመስል ነገር ነበረ።
am.R: ስመለከት ከሰሜን አውሎ ነፋስ ሲመጣ አየሁ። እሳት የሚብለጨለጭበት ትልቅ ደመና ነበረ፤ በዙሪያውም ደማቅ ብርሃን ያበራ ነበር። በእሳቱ መካከል የሚያበራ ብረት የሚመስል ነገር ነበረ።

hi.L: और मैंने देखा, और देखो, उत्तर दिशा से एक आँधी आ रही थी, एक बड़ा बादल, और आग जो बार-बार कौंध रही थी, और उसके चारों ओर चमक [थी], और उसके बीच में से, आग के बीच में से, दमकती धातु का-सा [कुछ] दिखाई देता था।
hi.B: मैंने देखा कि उत्तर से एक आँधी आ रही है: एक बहुत बड़ा बादल, जिसमें आग कौंध रही थी और जिसके चारों ओर चमक थी। आग के बीच में कुछ ऐसा था जो चमकती धातु-सा दिखाई देता था।
hi.R: मैंने देखा कि उत्तर की ओर से एक तूफ़ानी आँधी आ रही है। एक बहुत बड़ा बादल था, जिसमें आग कौंध रही थी, और उसके चारों ओर तेज़ रोशनी चमक रही थी। आग के बीच में कुछ ऐसा था जो चमकती धातु जैसा दिखता था।

ru.L: И я посмотрел, и вот, бурный ветер шёл с севера, великое облако и огонь, вспыхивающий [без перерыва], и сияние вокруг него, а из его середины [было нечто] как вид янтаря, из середины огня.
ru.B: Я посмотрел и увидел бурный ветер, шедший с севера: огромное облако, сквозь которое вспыхивал огонь, и сияние вокруг него. Посреди огня было что-то похожее на сверкающий металл.
ru.R: Я посмотрел и увидел, что с севера надвигается буря. Там было огромное облако, в нём вспыхивал огонь, а вокруг разливался яркий свет. Посреди огня было что-то похожее на блестящий металл.

ja.L: そしてわたしが見ると、なんと、激しい嵐の風が北から来ていた。大きな雲と、ひらめき続ける火があり、その周りには輝きがあった。そのただ中から、すなわち火のただ中から、琥珀の輝きのようなもの[が見えた]。
ja.B: わたしが見ていると、嵐の風が北から吹いて来るのが見えた。それは大きな雲で、その中を火がひらめき、周りには輝きがあった。その火のただ中には、輝く金属のようなものがあった。
ja.R: わたしが見ていると、北から大きな嵐がやって来るのが見えました。大きな雲があって、その中で火がひらめき、周りには明るい光が輝いていました。火の中には、光り輝く金属のようなものがありました。

uk.L: І я дивився, і ось — бурхливий вітер ішов з півночі, велика хмара, і вогонь, що спалахував, і сяйво [було] довкола неї, а з її середини — [щось] на вигляд, як бурштин, з середини вогню.
uk.B: Я дивився і побачив, як з півночі насувається буревій: величезна хмара, крізь яку спалахував вогонь, і сяйво довкола неї. Посеред вогню було щось схоже на блискучий метал.
uk.R: Я подивився і побачив буревій, що йшов з півночі. Там була величезна хмара, в якій спалахував вогонь, і яскраве світло сяяло довкола неї. Посеред вогню було щось схоже на сяючий метал.

decisions.choice: chashmal: a substance that shines brightly in fire; what it is, is uncertain
alternatives: electrum (an alloy of gold and silver)
decisions.reason: The word occurs only in Ezekiel (here, verse 27 and 8:2), and its meaning is not known. The setting shows that it gleams with a bright, fiery light. The Greek translation renders it with a word for electrum, an alloy of gold and silver, which was also the word for amber; later tradition followed it. Since the word cannot be pinned down, each rendering gives a general sense of brilliance.

decisions.choice: fire taking hold of itself: fire flashing back and forth without stopping
decisions.reason: The same unusual form is used of the fire that ran through the hail in Egypt (Exodus 9:24). It pictures flames, or lightning, catching and leaping again and again inside the cloud. Storm, cloud and fire are the signs of the LORD's coming in other places too (Exodus 19:16-18; Psalm 18:8-16).

decisions.choice: from the north: the direction from which judgment would come on Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Storms came from the north (Job 37:22), and so did the armies that invaded Israel. Jeremiah had seen disaster coming "from the north" on Jerusalem (Jeremiah 1:13-15). Here the LORD himself comes from that direction to meet the exiles in Babylon.

decisions.choice: amber (L); gleaming metal (B); shining metal (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *chashmal* in Ezekiel (1:4, 27; 8:2). Literal keeps the old rendering "amber", which goes back to the Greek. Balanced and Readable say "gleaming metal" and "shining metal", which give the brilliance the setting requires without claiming to know the substance (m1). A footnote gives the uncertainty.

decisions.choice: see (L); I saw (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word that points to something seen, traditionally "behold", is "see" at Literal. Balanced and Readable fold it into "I looked and saw". Balanced and Readable use "something that looked like" for "like the appearance of", the hedge set for this chapter (see 1:28).

decisions.choice: âmbar (L); metal reluzente (B); metal brilhante (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (1:4, 27; 8:2), as the English sets chashmal (r-en-1): Literal keeps the old rendering "âmbar", which goes back to the Greek; Balanced and Readable say what the reader needs to see, a metal shining in fire (m1). "Electro", the alloy the Greek may mean, is unknown to most readers.

decisions.choice: eis que (L); vi (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: hinneh in Ezekiel's visions is "eis" or "eis que" at Literal, the Portuguese word that copies it, as in Isaiah and Jeremiah. Balanced and Readable fold it into "olhei e vi", as the English does (r-en-2); in God's speeches it is "vejam"/"veja" or "Eu mesmo" as the English levels say.

decisions.choice: "ámbar" (L); "metal reluciente" (B); "metal brillante" (R)
decisions.reason: The substance is unknown; the levels follow the English choices, and the same words return in 1:27 and 8:2

decisions.choice: "Miré, y he aquí" (L); "Miré y vi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide wording for "and see" (hinneh) in the visions

decisions.choice: kaharabu (L); madini yanayong'aa (B); chuma kinachong'aa (R)
decisions.reason: What chashmal was is uncertain (meaning decision). Literal names a substance, amber, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable describe it as gleaming metal. The same words return at 1:27 and 8:2.

decisions.choice: "호박금" (L); "빛나는 금속" (B); "반짝이는 금속" (R)
decisions.reason: The substance is uncertain; "호박금" (electrum) keeps a single named substance at Literal, as the English "amber", and the other levels describe its shine. Used again at 1:27 and 8:2.

decisions.choice: hổ phách (L); kim loại sáng loáng (B); kim loại chiếu sáng (R)
decisions.reason: Nobody knows what chashmal was (see the meaning decision). Literal follows the English "amber"; Balanced and Readable describe what Ezekiel saw, a metal gleaming in fire. The same words are used in 1:27 and 8:2.

decisions.choice: "l'ambre" (Literal); "un métal étincelant" (Balanced); "un métal qui brille" (Readable), for chashmal in the whole book
decisions.reason: What the substance was is uncertain (the English meaning decision footnotes it). The French keeps the term sheet's three wordings, which match the English amber / gleaming metal / shining metal.

decisions.choice: "et voici" for hinneh (Literal); "je vis" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Voici" is the traditional French for the Hebrew pointer and reads naturally in a vision report; Balanced and Readable fold it into the verb of seeing, as the English does.

decisions.choice: chashmal "ቢጫ ዕንቁ" (Literal, a yellow gem, for the English "amber"); "የሚያንጸባርቅ ብረት" (Balanced); "የሚያበራ ብረት" (Readable)
decisions.reason: What the substance was is uncertain (the meaning decision). Each level follows its English: Literal names a shining yellow stone, as amber was valued, and Balanced and Readable say "gleaming / shining metal". The same wording is kept in 1:27 and 8:2.

decisions.choice: दमकती धातु (L); चमकती धातु (B, R)
decisions.reason: No one knows for certain what chashmal was (m1): a substance that shines in fire. The English Literal says "amber", but the Hindi word for amber (कहरुबा) is unfamiliar, so every level names what the reader is meant to see: a metal gleaming in the fire. The same words return in 1:27 and 8:2.

decisions.choice: देखो (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "and see" (hinneh) as देखो, as the earlier Hindi books do; Balanced and Readable fold it into "I saw".

decisions.choice: "янтарь" (L); "сверкающий металл" (B); "блестящий металл" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for chashmal in Ezekiel (1:4, 27; 8:2), as in English: Literal keeps the old rendering "янтарь"; Balanced and Readable describe what was seen, since what the substance is remains uncertain (m1).

decisions.choice: "вот" (L)
decisions.reason: The pointing word is "вот" at Literal, as for idou in the Gospels; Balanced and Readable fold it into "увидел".

decisions.choice: chashmal: "琥珀" (L), "輝く金属" (B), "光り輝く金属" (R), as the English amber / gleaming metal / shining metal; the same at 1:27 and 8:2.
decisions.reason: What the substance is, is uncertain (m1, footnoted); the Japanese follows each English level. "琥珀" is not Jōyō but is common and stays at Literal only.

decisions.choice: hinneh in Ezekiel's report: "なんと" (L); B, R "…のが見えた" as the English "I saw".
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings (no 見よ): "なんと" marks the surprise of what came into view.

decisions.choice: "бурштин" (L); "блискучий метал" (B); "сяючий метал" (R) for chashmal
decisions.reason: Following the Ezekiel terms table (uncertain): the word names something that gleams in the fire; Literal keeps the old reading "amber", the other levels describe it. Kept at 1:27 and 8:2.

en.R: Out of the middle of the fire came what looked like four living creatures. They were shaped like {{gender:human beings|men}},

ru.L: И из его середины — подобие четырёх живых существ, и вот [каков] их вид: подобие человека у них.
ru.B: Из середины его появилось нечто похожее на четыре живых существа. Вот как они выглядели: облик у них был человеческий.
ru.R: Из середины огня появилось что-то похожее на четыре живых существа. Они были похожи на людей,

ja.B: その中から、四つの生き物のようなものが現れた。その姿はこうであった。彼らは人間の形をしていた。

uk.L: І з її середини — подоба чотирьох живих істот, і ось [який] їхній вигляд: подоба людини в них.
uk.B: З її середини виходило щось схоже на чотири живі істоти. Ось який був їхній вигляд: вони мали подобу людини.
uk.R: Із середини вогню вийшло щось схоже на чотири живі істоти. Вони мали вигляд людей,

decisions.choice: living creatures: living beings, not yet named
decisions.reason: The word means simply living things, animals or creatures. Ezekiel does not name them here. When he sees them again in chapter 10 he recognizes them as cherubim (10:15, 20), the winged guardians of God's throne pictured over the ark of the covenant (Exodus 25:18-22).

decisions.choice: likeness: the first of the vision's hedges
decisions.reason: The word means a likeness or resemblance, something seen that is like something else. Ezekiel uses it, with "appearance", again and again through the chapter: he describes what he saw by comparing it with things he knew, and never claims that it simply was those things. See the note at 1:28.

decisions.choice: a human: a human being, not a man in particular
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a human being or humankind. It says that the creatures had a human shape, standing upright, before the faces and wings of verses 6-11 are described.

decisions.choice: something that looked like (B); what looked like (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Ezekiel keeps "the likeness of" at Literal and says "something that looked like" at Balanced and Readable, which keeps the hedge in plain words (see 1:28). Readable says "out of the middle of the fire" for "from its midst", from verse 4, and lets the sentence run on into verse 6.

decisions.choice: a human / a man (gender setting)
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, so the inclusive wording is the default and "a man", the traditional rendering, is the alternative, as in Revelation 4:7.

decisions.choice: os seres viventes (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (1:5-22; 3:13; 10:15, 17, 20): the creatures (m1) are "seres viventes" at every level, the name Revelation 4:6-9 gives them in Portuguese, which takes up this vision (1:10, m1). "Animais", the word of older versions, makes them beasts.

decisions.choice: a semelhança de (L); algo que parecia (B); o que parecia (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole vision, here and in chapters 8-10 and 40-48: Ezekiel's hedges (m2) are kept at every level, as the English keeps them (r-en-1). Literal keeps the nouns "semelhança" and "aparência"; Balanced and Readable say "algo que parecia", "o que parecia", "uma coisa que parecia", plain Portuguese that still does not say the thing simply was what it looked like.

decisions.choice: "seres vivientes"
decisions.reason: The word of Revelation 4:6 in Spanish, which draws on this vision

decisions.choice: "la semejanza de", "el aspecto de" (L); "algo que parecía", "lo que parecía" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide: every level keeps a hedge in the visions; B and R may shorten repeated hedges but never drop them

decisions.choice: mfano wa ... (L); kitu kilichoonekana kama ... (B, R); viumbe hai
alternatives: dropping the hedge at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Ezekiel hedges every description of what he sees (meaning decision at 1:28). Literal keeps "mfano wa", "sura ya" word for word; Balanced and Readable say "kitu kilichoonekana kama", something that looked like, and never drop the hedge. "Viumbe hai", living creatures, is the word of the published Revelation 4:6, used through chapters 1, 3 and 10.

decisions.choice: mwanadamu, wanadamu, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: The English offers "a human" / "a man" through the gender setting. Swahili "mwanadamu" already means a human being of either sex, and "mwanamume" would change the meaning, so Swahili has no gender span here or in the case law of chapters 3 and 18.

decisions.choice: "모양" for likeness, "모습" for appearance (L); "~처럼 보이는 것" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's hedges are kept at every level: Literal keeps the two Hebrew words apart ("모양", "모습"), and Balanced and Readable say "something that looked like", shortening but never dropping the hedge, through chapters 1, 8 and 10.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "사람" already means a human being of either sex, so Korean has only one wording and needs no gender span here or in 1:8, 1:10.

decisions.choice: con người, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "a human / a man" as a setting. Vietnamese "con người" (and "người" in verses 8 and 10) already means a human being of either sex, so there is nothing for a setting to change. The same holds through Ezekiel wherever the English has a gender span on "human".

decisions.choice: "les êtres vivants" at every level, for the whole book
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording, the same as the published Revelation 4-5, so a reader can see that John's four living creatures come from this vision.

decisions.choice: "la ressemblance de" (Literal); "quelque chose qui ressemblait à", "ce qui ressemblait à" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's hedges (likeness, appearance) are kept at every level, as the term sheet asks: Literal word for word, Balanced and Readable with "ressembler à". Readable never drops them.

decisions.choice: the living creatures (ḥayyot) "ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት", singular "ሕያው ፍጡር"; likeness (demut) "አምሳል" (Literal), "... የሚመስል" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት" is the word the Amharic Revelation 4:6-8 uses for the four creatures round the throne, which take up this vision; it is kept through chapters 1, 3 and 10. The vision's hedges keep a word for "likeness" or "looked like" at every level, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ሰው" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "a human / a man" as a reader setting; Amharic "ሰው" already means a human being of either sex, so it has nothing to switch. The same holds for the gender spans in verses 8 and 10.

decisions.choice: जीवित प्राणी (living creatures)
decisions.reason: The four are "living beings", not yet named (m1). जीवित प्राणी is the form Revelation 4:6 uses in Hindi for the four living creatures that come from this vision, so Ezekiel keeps it at every level. In chapter 10 they are named as करूब (cherubim), the form of Exodus 25 and 1 Kings 6.

decisions.choice: समानता ... रूप (L); कुछ ऐसा जो ... जैसा दिखता था (B, R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel hedges what he sees: "the likeness of", "the appearance of" (m2). Literal keeps the two nouns as समानता (likeness, demut) and रूप (appearance, mar'eh) every time; Balanced and Readable say "something that looked like", as the English does.

decisions.choice: मनुष्य, no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has a gender setting ("a human / a man"). Hindi मनुष्य already means a human being of either sex, so there is nothing for a setting to change and the Hindi has no span here or in 1:8 and 1:10.

decisions.choice: "живые существа" (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The form Revelation 4:6-8 uses for the same creatures in the Russian draft. The Synodal "животные" now means animals.

decisions.choice: "подобие" (L); "нечто похожее на" (B); "что-то похожее на" (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Ezekiel keeps the hedge "likeness" at every level: Literal "подобие", Balanced and Readable say it in plain words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "человек", with no gender span (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span here. Russian "человек" already means a human being of either sex, so no setting is needed, as in Revelation 4:7. The same holds in verses 8 and 10.

decisions.choice: chayyot "生き物" at every level, "四つの生き物" as Revelation 4:6; the vision's hedge demut "似姿" (L), "…のようなもの" (B, R).
decisions.reason: The creatures are not yet named (m1; they are cherubim in ch. 10); Revelation 4 Japanese has 四つの生き物. Ezekiel never says he saw the thing itself, so every level keeps a word of likeness (m2).

decisions.choice: 'adam "人間" with no gender span, where the English has {{gender:a human|a man's}}.
decisions.reason: "人間" is already inclusive, so Japanese needs no setting here (style 7a); the same for the human face and hands in 1:8 and 1:10.

decisions.choice: "людина" with no gender span, where the English has "a human" / "a man"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the general word for a human being (m3), and Ukrainian "людина" is already inclusive, so there is no second wording to offer (style guide section 7). The same holds through chapters 1 and 10.

decisions.choice: "живі істоти", as Revelation 4:6
decisions.reason: The Ukrainian Revelation uses "живі істоти" for the creatures that take up this vision; Ezekiel keeps the same words. The hedges ("подоба", "на вигляд", "щось схоже") are kept at every level, as the terms note asks.

source.text: וְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה פָנִ֖ים לְאֶחָ֑ת וְאַרְבַּ֥ע כְּנָפַ֖יִם לְאַחַ֥ת לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And four faces to [each] one, and four wings to [each] one of them.

en.L: And four faces [were] to each one, and four wings to each one of them.
en.B: Each of them had four faces and four wings.
en.R: but each one had four faces and four wings.

pt.L: E cada um [tinha] quatro rostos, e cada um deles, quatro asas.
pt.B: Cada um deles tinha quatro rostos e quatro asas.
pt.R: mas cada um tinha quatro rostos e quatro asas.

es.L: Y cuatro rostros tenía cada uno, y cuatro alas cada uno de ellos.
es.B: Cada uno tenía cuatro rostros y cuatro alas.
es.R: pero cada uno tenía cuatro rostros y cuatro alas.

sw.L: Na kila mmoja [alikuwa na] nyuso nne, na kila mmoja wao mabawa manne.
sw.B: Kila mmoja wao alikuwa na nyuso nne na mabawa manne.
sw.R: lakini kila mmoja alikuwa na nyuso nne na mabawa manne.

ko.L: 그리고 하나마다 네 얼굴이 있었고, 그들 하나마다 네 날개가 있었다.
ko.B: 그들은 저마다 얼굴이 넷이고 날개가 넷이었다.
ko.R: 저마다 얼굴이 넷, 날개가 넷이었다.

vi.L: Và mỗi [sinh vật] có bốn mặt, và mỗi [sinh vật] trong chúng có bốn cánh.
vi.B: Mỗi sinh vật có bốn mặt và bốn cánh.
vi.R: nhưng mỗi sinh vật có bốn mặt và bốn cánh.

fr.L: Et quatre faces [étaient] à chacun, et quatre ailes à chacun d’eux.
fr.B: Chacun d’eux avait quatre visages et quatre ailes.
fr.R: mais chacun avait quatre visages et quatre ailes.

am.L: ለእያንዳንዱም አራት ፊቶች፣ ለእያንዳንዳቸውም አራት ክንፎች [ነበሩ]።
am.B: እያንዳንዳቸው አራት ፊትና አራት ክንፍ ነበራቸው።
am.R: ነገር ግን እያንዳንዳቸው አራት ፊትና አራት ክንፍ ነበራቸው።

hi.L: और हर एक के चार मुख [थे], और उनमें से हर एक के चार पंख [थे]।
hi.B: उनमें से हर एक के चार मुख और चार पंख थे।
hi.R: पर हर एक के चार मुख और चार पंख थे।

ru.L: И четыре лица у каждого, и четыре крыла у каждого из них.
ru.B: У каждого из них было четыре лица и четыре крыла.
ru.R: но у каждого было четыре лица и четыре крыла.

ja.L: そしてそれぞれに四つの顔があり、彼らのそれぞれに四つの翼があった。
ja.B: それぞれが、四つの顔と四つの翼を持っていた。
ja.R: それぞれに、四つの顔と四つの翼がありました。

uk.L: І чотири обличчя в кожної, і чотири крила в кожної з них.
uk.B: Кожна з них мала чотири обличчя і чотири крила.
uk.R: але кожна мала чотири обличчя і чотири крила.

decisions.choice: four faces and four wings: a creature unlike any on earth
decisions.reason: Winged creatures with the bodies of several animals guarded thrones and temples in the art of the ancient Near East; the great winged bulls with human heads at the gates of Assyrian palaces are well known. Ezekiel's creatures go beyond anything in that art: each has four faces looking out in four directions (verse 10), so that it never has to turn (verse 9).

decisions.choice: but (R)
decisions.reason: Readable joins the verse to verse 5 with "but", because it has just said that the creatures were shaped like human beings, and the faces and wings are what made them different.

decisions.choice: "rostros"
decisions.reason: As the faces of the living creatures in Revelation 4:7

decisions.choice: "faces" (Literal); "visages" (Balanced, Readable), for the creatures' faces in the whole book
decisions.reason: "Face" is the older French for the face of a person or creature and keeps the Hebrew word visible at Literal; "visage" is what French says today.

source.text: וְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם רֶ֣גֶל יְשָׁרָ֑ה וְכַ֣ף רַגְלֵיהֶ֗ם כְּכַף֙ רֶ֣גֶל עֵ֔גֶל וְנֹ֣צְצִ֔ים כְּעֵ֖ין נְחֹ֥שֶׁת קָלָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And their feet [were] a foot straight, and [the] sole of their feet like [the] sole of [the] foot of a calf, and sparkling like [the] appearance of bronze burnished.

en.L: And their legs [were] straight legs, and the soles of their feet [were] like the sole of a calf's foot, and they were sparkling like the appearance of polished bronze.
en.B: Their legs were straight, and their feet were like a calf's hooves. They sparkled like polished bronze.
en.R: Their legs were straight. Their feet were like a calf's hooves, and they shone like polished bronze.

pt.L: E as suas pernas [eram] pernas retas, e a planta dos seus pés [era] como a planta do pé de um bezerro, e eles reluziam como a aparência de bronze polido.
pt.B: As pernas deles eram retas, e os pés eram como cascos de bezerro. Eles reluziam como bronze polido.
pt.R: As pernas deles eram retas. Os pés eram como cascos de bezerro e brilhavam como bronze polido.

es.L: Y sus piernas [eran] piernas rectas, y la planta de sus pies [era] como la planta del pie de un becerro, y centelleaban como el aspecto del bronce bruñido.
es.B: Sus piernas eran rectas, y sus pies eran como pezuñas de becerro. Centelleaban como bronce bruñido.
es.R: Sus piernas eran rectas. Sus pies eran como pezuñas de becerro y brillaban como bronce pulido.

sw.L: Na miguu yao [ilikuwa] miguu iliyonyooka, na nyayo za miguu yao [zilikuwa] kama wayo wa mguu wa ndama, nazo zilimetameta kama sura ya shaba iliyosuguliwa.
sw.B: Miguu yao ilikuwa imenyooka, na nyayo zao zilikuwa kama kwato za ndama. Zilimetameta kama shaba iliyosuguliwa.
sw.R: Miguu yao ilikuwa imenyooka. Nyayo zao zilikuwa kama kwato za ndama, nazo ziling'aa kama shaba iliyosuguliwa.

ko.L: 그리고 그들의 다리는 곧은 다리였고, 그들의 발바닥은 송아지 발바닥 같았으며, 빛나는 놋의 모습처럼 반짝이고 있었다.
ko.B: 그들의 다리는 곧았고, 발은 송아지 발굽 같았다. 그것들은 광을 낸 놋처럼 반짝였다.
ko.R: 그들의 다리는 곧았다. 발은 송아지 발굽 같았고, 반짝이게 닦은 놋처럼 빛났다.

vi.L: Và chân của chúng [là] chân thẳng, và bàn chân của chúng như bàn chân của con bò con, và chúng lấp lánh như diện mạo của đồng đánh bóng.
vi.B: Chân chúng thẳng, và bàn chân giống như móng chân bò con. Chúng lấp lánh như đồng đánh bóng.
vi.R: Chân chúng thẳng. Bàn chân chúng giống như móng bò con, và chúng sáng chói như đồng được đánh bóng.

fr.L: Et leurs jambes [étaient] des jambes droites, et la plante de leurs pieds [était] comme la plante du pied d’un veau, et ils étincelaient comme l’aspect du bronze poli.
fr.B: Leurs jambes étaient droites, et leurs pieds ressemblaient à des sabots de veau. Ils étincelaient comme du bronze poli.
fr.R: Leurs jambes étaient droites. Leurs pieds ressemblaient à des sabots de veau, et ils brillaient comme du bronze poli.

am.L: እግሮቻቸውም ቀጥ ያሉ እግሮች [ነበሩ]፤ የእግሮቻቸውም ኮቴ እንደ ጥጃ እግር ኮቴ [ነበረ]፤ እንደ ተወለወለ ነሐስ መልክም ያንጸባርቁ ነበር።
am.B: እግሮቻቸው ቀጥ ያሉ ነበሩ፤ ኮቴዎቻቸውም እንደ ጥጃ ኮቴ ነበሩ። እንደ ተወለወለ ነሐስም ያንጸባርቁ ነበር።
am.R: እግሮቻቸው ቀጥ ያሉ ነበሩ። ኮቴዎቻቸው እንደ ጥጃ ኮቴ ነበሩ፤ እንደ ተወለወለ ነሐስም ያበሩ ነበር።

hi.L: और उनके पाँव सीधे पाँव [थे], और उनके पाँवों के तलवे बछड़े के पाँव के तलवे के समान [थे], और वे झलकाए हुए पीतल के रूप के समान चमक रहे थे।
hi.B: उनके पाँव सीधे थे, और उनके पैर बछड़े के खुरों जैसे थे। वे झलकाए हुए पीतल की तरह चमकते थे।
hi.R: उनके पाँव सीधे थे। उनके पैर बछड़े के खुरों जैसे थे, और वे चमकाए हुए पीतल की तरह चमक रहे थे।

ru.L: И ноги их — прямые ноги, и ступни их ног — как ступня ноги телёнка, и сверкали они, как вид полированной бронзы.
ru.B: Ноги у них были прямые, а ступни — как копыта телёнка. Они сверкали, как полированная бронза.
ru.R: Ноги у них были прямые, а ступни — как копыта телёнка. Они блестели, как начищенная бронза.

ja.L: そして彼らの脚はまっすぐな脚で、彼らの足の裏は子牛の足の裏のようであり、磨いた青銅の輝きのようにきらめいていた。
ja.B: 脚はまっすぐで、足は子牛のひづめのようであった。それらは、磨いた青銅のようにきらめいていた。
ja.R: 脚はまっすぐでした。足は子牛のひづめのようで、磨いた青銅のように光っていました。

uk.L: А їхні ноги — ноги прямі, а підошви їхніх ніг — як підошва теляти, і вони виблискували, як вигляд полірованої бронзи.
uk.B: Їхні ноги були прямі, а ступні — як телячі копита. Вони виблискували, як полірована бронза.
uk.R: Їхні ноги були прямі. Їхні ступні були, як телячі копита, і сяяли, як полірована бронза.

decisions.choice: their legs were straight legs: the legs were straight and did not bend
decisions.reason: The same word means foot and leg. The first use here must be the whole leg, since it is called straight; the sole of the foot follows. Straight legs, perhaps with no bending joint, fit creatures that never turned as they moved (verses 9, 12) but went straight ahead.

decisions.choice: polished bronze: bronze burnished until it gleams
decisions.reason: The last word occurs only here and in Daniel 10:6, where the man in linen has arms and legs "like the gleam of burnished bronze". Revelation 1:15 takes up the picture.

decisions.choice: a calf's hooves (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the sole of a calf's foot". Balanced and Readable say "hooves", which is what a calf's foot is, and Readable says "shone" for "sparkled".

decisions.choice: "bronce bruñido" (L, B); "bronce pulido" (R)
decisions.reason: As Revelation 1:15 in Spanish

decisions.choice: झलकाए हुए पीतल (polished bronze)
decisions.reason: Hindi Bibles call bronze पीतल; "polished" is झलकाया हुआ (L, B) and चमकाया हुआ (R), as Revelation 1:15 describes the same metal.

decisions.choice: "бронза"
decisions.reason: Bronze, as in Revelation 1:15 in the Russian draft; the Synodal "медь" is copper.

source.text: וִידֵ֣י אָדָ֗ם מִתַּ֨חַת֙ כַּנְפֵיהֶ֔ם עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣עַת רִבְעֵיהֶ֑ם וּפְנֵיהֶ֥ם וְכַנְפֵיהֶ֖ם לְאַרְבַּעְתָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And hands of a human [were] under their wings on their four sides, and their faces and their wings [belonged] to the four of them.

en.L: And hands of {{gender:a human|a man}} [were] under their wings on their four sides, and the four of them [had] their faces and their wings [thus]:
en.B: Under their wings on their four sides they had {{gender:human hands|the hands of a man}}. As for the faces and wings of the four of them,
en.R: Under their wings, on all four sides, they had {{gender:human hands|hands like a man's}}. All four creatures had faces and wings.

pt.L: E mãos de {{gender:um ser humano|um homem}} [estavam] debaixo das suas asas, nos seus quatro lados; e os quatro [tinham] os seus rostos e as suas asas [assim]:
pt.B: Debaixo das asas, nos quatro lados, eles tinham {{gender:mãos humanas|mãos de homem}}. Quanto aos rostos e às asas dos quatro,
pt.R: Debaixo das asas, nos quatro lados, eles tinham {{gender:mãos humanas|mãos como as de um homem}}. Todos os quatro seres tinham rostos e asas.

es.L: Y manos de {{gender:ser humano|hombre}} [había] debajo de sus alas, en sus cuatro lados; y los cuatro [tenían] sus rostros y sus alas [así]:
es.B: Debajo de sus alas, en sus cuatro lados, tenían {{gender:manos humanas|manos de hombre}}. En cuanto a los rostros y las alas de los cuatro,
es.R: Debajo de sus alas, en los cuatro lados, tenían {{gender:manos humanas|manos como de hombre}}. Los cuatro seres tenían rostros y alas.

sw.L: Na mikono ya mwanadamu [ilikuwa] chini ya mabawa yao pande zao nne, nao wanne [walikuwa na] nyuso zao na mabawa yao [hivi]:
sw.B: Chini ya mabawa yao, pande zao nne, walikuwa na mikono ya kibinadamu. Kuhusu nyuso na mabawa ya wale wanne,
sw.R: Chini ya mabawa yao, pande zote nne, walikuwa na mikono kama ya wanadamu. Viumbe wote wanne walikuwa na nyuso na mabawa.

ko.L: 그리고 그들의 날개 아래 네 면에 사람의 손이 있었고, 그 넷은 그들의 얼굴과 그들의 날개가 [이러했다].
ko.B: 그들의 날개 아래 네 면에는 사람의 손이 있었다. 그 넷의 얼굴과 날개를 말하자면,
ko.R: 날개 아래 네 면에는 사람의 손이 있었다. 네 생물은 모두 얼굴과 날개가 있었다.

vi.L: Và tay của con người [ở] dưới cánh chúng, trên bốn phía của chúng; và bốn [sinh vật] ấy [có] mặt và cánh của mình [như sau]:
vi.B: Dưới cánh, ở cả bốn phía, chúng có tay như tay người. Còn về mặt và cánh của bốn sinh vật ấy thì
vi.R: Dưới cánh, ở cả bốn phía, chúng có tay giống như tay người. Cả bốn sinh vật đều có mặt và cánh.

fr.L: Et des mains d’{{gender:un être humain|un homme}} [étaient] sous leurs ailes, sur leurs quatre côtés ; et les quatre avaient leurs faces et leurs ailes [ainsi] :
fr.B: Sous leurs ailes, sur leurs quatre côtés, ils avaient des mains {{gender:humaines|d’homme}}. Quant aux visages et aux ailes des quatre,
fr.R: Sous leurs ailes, sur les quatre côtés, ils avaient des mains {{gender:humaines|comme celles d’un homme}}. Les quatre êtres avaient des visages et des ailes.

am.L: ከክንፎቻቸውም በታች በአራቱ ጎኖቻቸው የሰው እጆች [ነበሩ]፤ የአራቱም ፊቶቻቸውና ክንፎቻቸው [እንዲህ ነበሩ]፤
am.B: ከክንፎቻቸው በታች በአራቱም ጎኖቻቸው የሰው እጆች ነበሯቸው። የአራቱን ፊቶችና ክንፎች በተመለከተ፣
am.R: ከክንፎቻቸው በታች በአራቱም ጎኖች የሰው እጆች ነበሯቸው። አራቱም ፍጥረታት ፊቶችና ክንፎች ነበሯቸው።

hi.L: और उनके चारों ओर उनके पंखों के नीचे मनुष्य के हाथ [थे], और उन चारों के मुख और पंख [इस प्रकार थे]:
hi.B: उनके पंखों के नीचे, चारों ओर, उनके मनुष्य जैसे हाथ थे। उन चारों के मुखों और पंखों के विषय में,
hi.R: उनके पंखों के नीचे, चारों ओर, उनके मनुष्यों जैसे हाथ थे। चारों प्राणियों के मुख और पंख थे।

ru.L: И руки человека [были] под их крыльями на четырёх их сторонах, и у четырёх их — лица их и крылья их [таковы]:
ru.B: Под крыльями, на всех четырёх сторонах, у них были человеческие руки. Что же до лиц и крыльев всех четырёх,
ru.R: Под крыльями, со всех четырёх сторон, у них были человеческие руки. У всех четырёх существ были лица и крылья.

ja.L: そして彼らの翼の下、その四つの側には人間の手があった。そして四つ[の生き物]は、その顔と翼を[次のように]持っていた。
ja.B: 翼の下には、四つの側に人間の手があった。四つの生き物の顔と翼は、次のようであった。
ja.R: 翼の下には、四つの側のどこにも、人間の手がありました。四つの生き物は、どれも顔と翼を持っていました。

uk.L: І руки людини [були] під їхніми крилами з їхніх чотирьох боків, і в усіх чотирьох — їхні обличчя і їхні крила [такі]:
uk.B: Під крилами з чотирьох боків вони мали людські руки. А щодо облич і крил усіх чотирьох,
uk.R: Під крилами, з усіх чотирьох боків, вони мали людські руки. Усі чотири істоти мали обличчя і крила.

decisions.choice: and hands: the reading tradition, against the written "and his hands"
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text read "and his hands", but the scribes' marginal note tells the reader to say "and hands of", which fits the phrase "hands of a human". The reading in the margin is followed. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the four of them had their faces and their wings: a heading for what follows
decisions.reason: The last clause names the faces and wings again, and verses 9-11 describe them: first the wings (verse 9), then the faces (verse 10), then the wings again (verse 11). It is best read as introducing that description.

decisions.choice: human hands / hands of a man (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the word means a human being, so the inclusive wording is the default. Balanced lets the sentence run on into verse 9, as the Hebrew does; Readable makes the last clause a sentence of its own.

source.text: חֹֽבְרֹ֛ת אִשָּׁ֥ה אֶל־אֲחוֹתָ֖הּ כַּנְפֵיהֶ֑ם לֹא־יִסַּ֣בּוּ בְלֶכְתָּ֔ן אִ֛ישׁ אֶל־עֵ֥בֶר פָּנָ֖יו יֵלֵֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [were] joined a woman to her sister their wings; not they turned when they went; each in the direction of his face they went.

en.L: Their wings [were] touching each one its sister; they did not turn when they went; each went in the direction of its face.
en.B: their wings touched one another. As they moved they did not turn; each of them went straight ahead.
en.R: Each creature's wings touched the wings of the creature next to it. When they moved, they did not turn around. Each one went straight forward.

pt.L: As suas asas [estavam] tocando cada uma a sua irmã; não se viravam quando andavam; cada um andava na direção do seu rosto.
pt.B: as suas asas se tocavam umas nas outras. Ao se moverem, não se viravam; cada um deles ia sempre em frente.
pt.R: As asas de cada ser tocavam as asas do ser que estava ao lado. Quando eles se moviam, não se viravam. Cada um ia sempre para a frente.

es.L: Sus alas [estaban] unidas cada una con su hermana; no se volvían cuando andaban; cada uno andaba en la dirección de su rostro.
es.B: sus alas se tocaban unas con otras. Al moverse no se volvían; cada uno iba de frente.
es.R: Las alas de cada ser tocaban las alas del ser que estaba a su lado. Cuando se movían, no se daban la vuelta. Cada uno iba derecho hacia adelante.

sw.L: mabawa yao yaligusana, moja na dada yake; hawakugeuka walipokwenda; kila mmoja alikwenda upande wa uso wake.
sw.B: mabawa yao yaligusana. Walipokwenda hawakugeuka; kila mmoja alikwenda moja kwa moja mbele.
sw.R: Mabawa ya kila kiumbe yaligusa mabawa ya kiumbe aliyekuwa karibu naye. Walipokwenda, hawakugeuka. Kila mmoja alikwenda moja kwa moja mbele.

ko.L: 그들의 날개는 하나가 다른 하나에 닿아 있었다. 그들은 갈 때에 돌지 않았고, 저마다 자기 얼굴이 향한 쪽으로 갔다.
ko.B: 날개가 서로 맞닿아 있었다. 그들은 움직일 때 몸을 돌리지 않고 저마다 앞으로 곧장 나아갔다.
ko.R: 각 생물의 날개는 옆에 있는 생물의 날개에 닿아 있었다. 그들은 움직일 때 몸을 돌리지 않았다. 저마다 앞으로 곧장 나아갔다.

vi.L: cánh của chúng chạm vào nhau, cánh này với cánh kia; chúng không quay lại khi đi; mỗi [sinh vật] đi theo hướng mặt mình.
vi.B: cánh của chúng chạm vào nhau. Khi di chuyển, chúng không quay mình; mỗi sinh vật cứ đi thẳng tới trước.
vi.R: Cánh của mỗi sinh vật chạm vào cánh của sinh vật bên cạnh. Khi di chuyển, chúng không quay lại. Mỗi sinh vật cứ đi thẳng tới trước.

fr.L: leurs ailes [étaient] jointes l’une à sa sœur ; ils ne se tournaient pas quand ils allaient ; chacun allait droit devant sa face.
fr.B: leurs ailes se touchaient l’une l’autre. En avançant, ils ne se tournaient pas : chacun allait droit devant lui.
fr.R: Les ailes de chaque être touchaient les ailes de l’être voisin. Quand ils avançaient, ils ne se retournaient pas. Chacun allait tout droit.

am.L: ክንፎቻቸው እያንዳንዱ ከእኅቱ ጋር የተገናኘ [ነበረ]፤ ሲሄዱም አይዞሩም ነበር፤ እያንዳንዱ ወደ ፊቱ አቅጣጫ ይሄድ ነበር።
am.B: ክንፎቻቸው እርስ በርሳቸው ይነካኩ ነበር። ሲንቀሳቀሱ አይዞሩም ነበር፤ እያንዳንዳቸው በቀጥታ ወደ ፊት ይሄዱ ነበር።
am.R: የእያንዳንዱ ፍጡር ክንፎች ከአጠገቡ ካለው ፍጡር ክንፎች ጋር ይነካኩ ነበር። ሲንቀሳቀሱ አይዞሩም ነበር። እያንዳንዱ በቀጥታ ወደ ፊት ይሄድ ነበር።

hi.L: उनके पंख एक दूसरे से, हर एक अपनी बहन से, मिले हुए [थे]; चलते समय वे मुड़ते नहीं थे; हर एक अपने मुख की दिशा में चलता था।
hi.B: उनके पंख एक दूसरे को छूते थे। चलते समय वे मुड़ते नहीं थे; हर एक सीधा आगे चलता था।
hi.R: हर प्राणी के पंख उसके पास वाले प्राणी के पंखों को छूते थे। जब वे चलते थे, तो पीछे नहीं मुड़ते थे। हर एक सीधा आगे ही चलता था।

ru.L: Крылья их соприкасались, каждое — со своей сестрой; не поворачивались они, когда шли; каждое шло в сторону своего лица.
ru.B: их крылья касались друг друга. Двигаясь, они не поворачивались: каждое шло прямо вперёд.
ru.R: Крылья каждого существа касались крыльев соседнего. Когда они двигались, они не поворачивались. Каждое шло прямо вперёд.

ja.L: 彼らの翼は、互いに一つが他の一つに触れ合っていた。彼らは進むとき向きを変えなかった。それぞれ自分の顔の向いている方へ進んだ。
ja.B: 翼は互いに触れ合っていた。進むときに向きを変えることはなく、それぞれまっすぐ前へ進んだ。
ja.R: それぞれの生き物の翼は、隣の生き物の翼に触れていました。進むとき、向きを変えることはありませんでした。それぞれが、まっすぐ前へ進みました。

uk.L: Їхні крила торкалися одне одного; вони не поверталися, коли йшли; кожна йшла в напрямку свого обличчя.
uk.B: їхні крила торкалися одне одного. Рухаючись, вони не поверталися; кожна йшла просто вперед.
uk.R: Крила кожної істоти торкалися крил сусідньої істоти. Коли вони рухалися, то не оберталися. Кожна йшла просто вперед.

decisions.choice: a woman to her sister: one another
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses "a man ... his brother" for "one another", and "a woman ... her sister" when the nouns are feminine, as "wings" is here. Nothing about women is meant. The wings of each creature touched those of the creatures beside it, so that the four formed one square.

decisions.choice: each went in the direction of its face: they could go any way without turning
decisions.reason: Each creature had a face toward each of the four directions (verse 10). Whichever way they went, a face was looking that way, so they moved straight ahead without turning (verses 12, 17).

decisions.choice: each one its sister (L); one another (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1). Readable spells out whose wings touched whose.

decisions.choice: cánh này với cánh kia (L)
alternatives: cánh này với chị em của nó
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom "a woman to her sister" means "one another". Vietnamese "chị em" said of wings would read as a picture the Hebrew does not intend, so even Literal gives the sense; the meaning decision gives the idiom. The same in verse 23.

decisions.choice: हर एक अपनी बहन से (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a woman to her sister", an idiom for "one another" (m1). Literal keeps the image after एक दूसरे से, since पंख is masculine in Hindi and the idiom would otherwise be unclear; Balanced and Readable say only "one another".

decisions.choice: "каждое — со своей сестрой" (L); "друг друга" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom ("a woman to her sister"), as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: 'ishshah 'el-'achotah ("a woman to her sister") "一つが他の一つに" at Literal, not "女がその姉妹に".
decisions.reason: The idiom means "one another" (m1) and is used of feminine things; a word-for-word 姉妹 would read as women in Japanese.

source.text: וּדְמ֣וּת פְּנֵיהֶם֮ פְּנֵ֣י אָדָם֒ וּפְנֵ֨י אַרְיֵ֤ה אֶל־הַיָּמִין֙ לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֔ם וּפְנֵי־שׁ֥וֹר מֵֽהַשְּׂמֹ֖אול לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֑ן וּפְנֵי־נֶ֖שֶׁר לְאַרְבַּעְתָּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] likeness of their faces: [the] face of a human, and [the] face of a lion to the right [belonged] to the four of them, and [the] face of an ox from the left [belonged] to the four of them, and [the] face of an eagle [belonged] to the four of them.

en.L: And the likeness of their faces: [each had] the face of {{gender:a human|a man}}, and the face of a lion [was] on the right for the four of them, and the face of an ox on the left for the four of them, and the face of an eagle for the four of them.
en.B: This is what their faces looked like: each of the four had {{gender:a human face|the face of a man}}, the face of a lion on the right, the face of an ox on the left, and the face of an eagle.
en.R: This is what their faces looked like. Each of the four had {{gender:a human face|a man's face}} in front. It had a lion's face on the right side and an ox's face on the left side. It also had an eagle's face.

pt.L: E a semelhança dos seus rostos: [cada um tinha] o rosto de {{gender:um ser humano|um homem}}, e o rosto de um leão à direita nos quatro, e o rosto de um boi à esquerda nos quatro, e o rosto de uma águia nos quatro.
pt.B: Os rostos deles eram assim: cada um dos quatro tinha {{gender:um rosto humano|um rosto de homem}}, um rosto de leão à direita, um rosto de boi à esquerda e um rosto de águia.
pt.R: Os rostos deles eram assim. Cada um dos quatro tinha {{gender:um rosto humano|um rosto de homem}} na frente. Tinha um rosto de leão do lado direito e um rosto de boi do lado esquerdo. Também tinha um rosto de águia.

es.L: Y la semejanza de sus rostros: [cada uno tenía] rostro de {{gender:ser humano|hombre}}, y rostro de león a la derecha los cuatro, y rostro de buey a la izquierda los cuatro, y rostro de águila los cuatro.
es.B: Este era el aspecto de sus rostros: cada uno de los cuatro tenía {{gender:rostro humano|rostro de hombre}}, rostro de león a la derecha, rostro de buey a la izquierda, y rostro de águila.
es.R: Así eran sus rostros: cada uno de los cuatro tenía {{gender:un rostro humano|un rostro de hombre}} por delante. Tenía un rostro de león en el lado derecho y un rostro de buey en el lado izquierdo. También tenía un rostro de águila.

sw.L: Na mfano wa nyuso zao: [kila mmoja alikuwa na] uso wa mwanadamu, na uso wa simba upande wa kulia kwa wote wanne, na uso wa ng'ombe upande wa kushoto kwa wote wanne, na uso wa tai kwa wote wanne.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo nyuso zao zilivyoonekana: kila mmoja wa wale wanne alikuwa na uso wa mwanadamu, uso wa simba upande wa kulia, uso wa ng'ombe upande wa kushoto, na uso wa tai.
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo nyuso zao zilivyoonekana. Kila mmoja wa wale wanne alikuwa na uso wa mwanadamu mbele. Alikuwa na uso wa simba upande wa kulia na uso wa ng'ombe upande wa kushoto. Pia alikuwa na uso wa tai.

ko.L: 그리고 그들의 얼굴의 모양은 [이러했다]. 사람의 얼굴이 [있었고], 넷의 오른쪽에는 사자의 얼굴이, 넷의 왼쪽에는 소의 얼굴이 있었으며, 넷에게 독수리의 얼굴이 있었다.
ko.B: 그들의 얼굴 모습은 이러했다. 넷이 저마다 사람의 얼굴을 하고 있었고, 오른쪽에는 사자의 얼굴, 왼쪽에는 소의 얼굴, 그리고 독수리의 얼굴이 있었다.
ko.R: 그들의 얼굴은 이렇게 생겼다. 넷이 모두 앞쪽에 사람의 얼굴이 있었다. 오른쪽에는 사자의 얼굴, 왼쪽에는 소의 얼굴이 있었다. 또 독수리의 얼굴도 있었다.

vi.L: Và hình dạng của mặt chúng: [mỗi sinh vật có] mặt của con người, và mặt sư tử ở bên phải của bốn [sinh vật], và mặt bò ở bên trái của bốn [sinh vật], và mặt chim đại bàng của bốn [sinh vật].
vi.B: Mặt của chúng trông như thế này: cả bốn sinh vật đều có mặt người, mặt sư tử ở bên phải, mặt bò ở bên trái, và mặt chim đại bàng.
vi.R: Mặt của chúng trông như thế này. Mỗi sinh vật có một mặt người ở phía trước. Bên phải có mặt sư tử, bên trái có mặt bò. Nó cũng có mặt chim đại bàng.

fr.L: Et la ressemblance de leurs faces : [chacun avait] une face d’{{gender:être humain|homme}}, et une face de lion à droite pour les quatre, et une face de bœuf à gauche pour les quatre, et une face d’aigle pour les quatre.
fr.B: Voici à quoi ressemblaient leurs visages : chacun des quatre avait un visage {{gender:humain|d’homme}}, un visage de lion à droite, un visage de bœuf à gauche, et un visage d’aigle.
fr.R: Voici à quoi ressemblaient leurs visages. Chacun des quatre avait un visage {{gender:humain|d’homme}} devant. Il avait un visage de lion du côté droit et un visage de bœuf du côté gauche. Il avait aussi un visage d’aigle.

am.L: የፊቶቻቸውም አምሳል [ይህ ነበረ]፤ [እያንዳንዳቸው] የሰው ፊት [ነበራቸው]፤ ለአራቱም በቀኝ በኩል የአንበሳ ፊት፣ ለአራቱም በግራ በኩል የበሬ ፊት፣ ለአራቱም የንስር ፊት [ነበራቸው]።
am.B: የፊቶቻቸው መልክ ይህ ነበረ፤ ከአራቱ እያንዳንዳቸው የሰው ፊት፣ በቀኝ በኩል የአንበሳ ፊት፣ በግራ በኩል የበሬ ፊት፣ እንዲሁም የንስር ፊት ነበራቸው።
am.R: ፊቶቻቸው እንዲህ ይመስሉ ነበር። ከአራቱ እያንዳንዳቸው በፊት በኩል የሰው ፊት ነበራቸው። በቀኝ በኩል የአንበሳ ፊት፣ በግራ በኩል ደግሞ የበሬ ፊት ነበራቸው። በተጨማሪም የንስር ፊት ነበራቸው።

hi.L: और उनके मुखों की समानता: [हर एक का] मनुष्य का मुख [था], और उन चारों के दाहिनी ओर सिंह का मुख [था], और उन चारों के बाईं ओर बैल का मुख, और उन चारों के उकाब का मुख [था]।
hi.B: उनके मुख ऐसे दिखते थे: उन चारों में से हर एक का मनुष्य का मुख था, दाहिनी ओर सिंह का मुख, बाईं ओर बैल का मुख, और उकाब का मुख।
